_comment: Season System Spec §14 — The Effectiveness System. Scope: Season 1 content only (open question #38) — grades every monster `type` value that exists on the 41 anime bosses today, plus the Season 1 dungeon's own enemies, against the four move CATEGORIES a player can actually choose from in combat (per §14.1: attack, skill, character ability, weapon effect). Basis: monster TYPE as default (open question #34), no per-monster-id overrides yet — the table is small enough that per-monster exceptions can be layered in later under `overrides` without a shape change. Scale: numeric multiplier (open question #35) — 0.5x / 1x / 1.25x / 1.5x / 2x, chosen over Pokémon-style tiers because attack.js/ability-engine.js already multiply raw damage by a float (calcPlayerDamage's damageMultiplier param), so a numeric grade drops straight into that pipeline with zero translation. Application: advisory-only for Willow, does NOT touch combat-engine.js damage math (open question #36) — no player asked for a Willow readout to secretly change what their basic attack rolls, and changing live damage math for 8 monster types under 4 move categories is a much bigger, separate balance pass than 'ship Willow'.

_matchup_notes: weakTo/resistTo already authored per-boss in bosses/*.js (e.g. aizen_sosuke: weakTo ['holy'], resistTo ['physical','magic','shadow','holy','fire','ice']) push the grade one full step further in the listed direction on top of the base `type` grade below — see lib/effectiveness-engine.js gradeMove(). A boss's own weakTo/resistTo always wins over the base table entry for its type when they conflict.

season01Enemies._comment: Type/weakTo/resistTo assigned to the Season 1 dungeon roster (data/monsters.json season_01_ruins entries) so gradeMove() has real per-monster data to read for every enemy in the new dungeon, not just the 41 anime bosses.
